findings.title: HSBC picks the UAE to launch its first "immediately international" account
findings.summary: HSBC UAE became the first market in HSBC's global network to launch the upgraded Premier Global Money Account, a fully integrated multi-currency account and linked Visa debit card that is international by default from the moment a customer is onboarded. Customers hold, spend, transfer and receive in 20+ currencies under a single IBAN with no HSBC fees on supported currencies, removing the usual friction of separate accounts, activation steps and FX timing. The CX read-across matters more than the product: HSBC explicitly chose the UAE ahead of every other market in its network because a majority of residents already transact in multiple currencies, and the proposition is expected to reach other HSBC markets over the next one to two years. UAE Chief Executive Mohamed Al Marzooqi tied it to "continued investment in new, state-of-the-art wealth centres", i.e. a combined digital-and-physical service model, not a digital-only play. For MECSC members, this is a clean example of a global brand treating the Gulf as its lead customer-experience market rather than a follower market.

findings.title: Loyalty & Reward Co opens Dubai office as regional loyalty market heads for US$5.6bn
findings.summary: The global pure-play loyalty consultancy opened a Dubai office and appointed Krishna Mohan as Loyalty Director (MENA). Mohan brings two decades of GCC loyalty and CRM leadership, he scaled Shukran Rewards at Landmark Group, launched the Blue Rewards ecosystem at Al-Futtaim, and most recently led the evolution of Nahdi's Nuhdeek programme across KSA and the UAE. The firm targets MENA at 20% of global revenue by 2028. The market framing is the useful part. Middle East loyalty is forecast to grow from US$3.4bn in 2026 to US$5.6bn by 2030 (12.8% CAGR), with the UAE reaching US$592.4m and Saudi Arabia US$1.27bn. The firm identifies five shifts relevant to mall and retail operators: rewards moving to everyday journeys (fuel, grocery, mobility, bill payment); AI-driven personalisation at scale across physical and digital channels; loyalty embedded inside national wallets and payment apps, with a warning that "programs without payment integration risk losing relevance"; large regional groups consolidating multi-brand ecosystems so members earn and redeem across grocery, malls, fashion, dining and entertainment; and e-commerce/quick-commerce platforms building their own loyalty layers to escape discounting.

findings.title: Salesforce State of Commerce: UAE commerce leaders put AI first, but omnichannel still breaks
findings.summary: Labelled Recent Background, published 11 August, outside the coverage window but directly relevant to both streams and not previously expanded in detail. Implementing or expanding AI now ranks as the number one priority for UAE commerce leaders, ahead of growing the customer base. 62% have optimised content for conversational and question-based queries, 61% improved product content quality, 58% submit data feeds directly to AI search platforms, and 31% monitor how their brands appear in AI-generated responses. The failure points are the CX story: for UAE B2B organisations, ordering channels siloed across multiple systems is the most common breakdown (44%), followed by inventory data not synchronised in real time (37%), inability to recognise customer information consistently across channels (35%) and inconsistent returns/exchanges (35%). Only 1% of UAE multichannel organisations report no significant breakdowns at all. Among UAE organisations that have unified customer data, 48% report improved AI and automation outcomes, 43% higher conversion, 43% better retention and 41% faster issue resolution.

findings.title: The agentic CX scorecard changes: containment out, proven resolution in
findings.summary: CX Today's analysis of three simultaneous vendor moves, ServiceNow's Autonomous Workforce, Salesforce's Headless 360 expansion and Synthflow's voice-AI resolution push, argues that AI in customer experience has passed the point where a good conversation is enough. The new test is whether an AI agent actually completed the customer's task, operated within policy, and left a clean route to human recovery when it failed. Three points worth carrying into member conversations. First, the commercial signal is real but not proof of capability: ServiceNow reports AI annual contract value above US$1bn and a ninefold increase in agentic deployments in nine months, buyer intent, not evidence that autonomous service works consistently in complex environments. Second, workforce planning breaks: removing simple contacts leaves human agents with complaints, exceptions, sensitive cases and journeys where AI already failed once, so forecasting now needs AI completion rates, failed-action rates, transfer rates and repeat contacts as inputs. Third, Salesforce's MCP-based architecture (Data 360 exposing roughly 200 APIs, with agents inheriting existing object relationships, validation rules and permissions) is architecturally significant but inherits weaknesses too, "poorly defined permissions, fragmented customer data, inconsistent business rules... will travel with the agent." ServiceNow's Amit Zavery put the shift bluntly: "Advisory AI has run its course; enterprises need AI that senses, decides, and securely acts in accordance with organizational guardrails." findings.title: Verizon and Google Cloud put agentic AI behind 28,000 customer-care reps
findings.summary: Verizon announced a strategic partnership with Google Cloud to expand Gemini Enterprise, modernise enterprise data and scale AI across customer service, network operations, marketing and employee workflows. The conversational agent, built on Vertex AI, Gemini models and the Agent Assist panel, supports 28,000 customer-care representatives and retail stores, functioning as a "personal research assistant" that anticipates customer needs. A separate "problem solver agent" guides reps through advanced troubleshooting on complex queries rather than simply returning an answer. Verizon claims the partnership has produced "95 percent comprehensive answerability for customer inquiries". The deliberate design choice is the transferable lesson for GCC telecoms and large retailers: AI absorbs the volume of everyday interactions while human support is reserved for moments that are complicated, sensitive, or likely to damage loyalty, an assist-first model rather than a deflection-first one.

findings.title: Historic context: Ooredoo Qatar's Gemini Enterprise deployment
findings.summary: Labelled Historic Context, published 27 November 2025, well outside the window. Ooredoo Qatar deployed Gemini Enterprise company-wide, becoming one of the first telecom operators in EMEA to adopt Google Cloud's agentic AI platform, with teams using it to personalise customer interactions and marketing/creative teams adopting Veo, Imagen and Gemini Flash Image. Included only because it directly prefigures the Verizon announcement above, the same platform, the same customer-care logic, deployed in the GCC nine months earlier.

findings.title: RTIH launches the inaugural Retail Technology Hot 100
findings.summary: The Retail Technology Innovation Hub published its first-ever Hot 100 list, positioning AI, computer vision, robotics, inventory intelligence and digital infrastructure as the foundations of modern retail rather than as add-ons. The accompanying commentary stresses that agentic commerce only works where AI agents operate from trusted, real-time, deterministic data, a data-quality argument that lines up closely with the Salesforce omnichannel breakdown figures in Section A. Useful as a scanning list for mall operators and retail members assessing which technology categories are maturing beyond pilot stage.

findings.title: Dubai community retail: The Grand opens in phases, eight more destinations behind it
findings.summary: Labelled Recent Background, published 1 August. The Grand at Nad Al Sheba Gardens began a phased opening on 19 August, fully leased and anchored by the first Waitrose & Partners in the community, with dining, wellness and pharmacy tenants (Tashas, Somewhere, Home Bakery, Kokoro, Staywell Pharmacy, Tips & Toes) following from early September and healthcare (Fitcode, American Hospital) in early 2027. The experience angle: a fully-leased everyday-services mix, grocery, healthcare, nursery, optical, wellness, rather than a fashion-led format. Behind it sit eight further Dubai destinations, including Sobha Mall (H2 2026), two Le Meryeme community malls, South Bay Mall, Ghaf Woods Mall (forest-integrated, moving away from the enclosed-mall format) and Dubai Square. Existing centres are expanding too: Dh1.5bn at Dubai Mall (240 luxury retail and dining outlets) and Dh5bn at Mall of the Emirates (100 stores plus an indoor-outdoor dining precinct, a luxury wellness club, a cultural hub and the world's most advanced IMAX at VOX, with an outdoor greenery-covered F&B courtyard due early 2027).

findings.title: Historic context: Aventura Mall, Kuwait (opening this quarter)
findings.summary: Labelled Historic Context, announced 13 May 2026. Mabanee signed Alshaya Group for 20+ stores across 10,000+ sq m at Aventura Mall in Jaber Al-Ahmad City, delivered under a public-private partnership with National Industries Company and Privatization Holding. Aventura Mall is scheduled to open in Q3 2026, i.e. within weeks, with Ulta Beauty following in Q4 2026 and Primark in Q1 2027. Flagged now as a near-term watch item rather than as news.

findings.title: Ulta Beauty opens third UAE store at Dubai Hills Mall
findings.summary: Ulta Beauty has opened its third United Arab Emirates location at Emaar's Dubai Hills Mall, following earlier launches at Mall of the Emirates and The Dubai Mall. The store trades under the retailer's regional franchise partnership with Alshaya Group. More than 20 brands new to the Ulta Beauty Middle East line-up have been added at Dubai Hills across make-up, skincare, haircare, fragrance and wellness, including wellness names Cymbiotika, Vida Glow, Mims, SYP and Nutrili, and regional labels Clara, SADE and Ojar. Dubai-based creator Daniah Fawaz's brand Kyza has launched exclusively at Ulta Beauty, alongside Carolina Herrera Makeup, Nest, MDF Skincare and Lonvitalite Skincare. Rebecca Jobo, President of Wellness at Alshaya Group, attributed the pace of rollout to a "strong response from customers." Distinct from the previously-reported Ulta Beauty UAE market entry at Mall of the Emirates (Jan 2026) and the announced Ulta debut within Doha Festival City's QR400m transformation in Qatar (carried 21 Aug).

findings.title: Volvo Cars Bahrain opens brand boutique at Marassi Galleria
findings.summary: Volvo Cars Bahrain, operating under Motorcity Bahrain, has opened a brand boutique inside Marassi Galleria, located near Gate 1. The mall-format retail unit displays the 2026 Volvo XC90, ES90 and EX30 and offers personalised product consultations rather than a conventional dealership experience. Ghassan Freiwat, Chief Strategy Officer at Motorcity Bahrain, framed the boutique as a way of "bringing the Volvo experience closer to our customers." An opening campaign bundles a three-year / 45,000 km service package and a two-person stay at Address Beach Resort Bahrain with purchases of 2026 models. Logged as a tenancy/status update for Marassi Galleria, and a further data point on automotive-brand take-up of mall space in the Bahraini market.

findings.title: Mothercare to open new store at Purple Mall, Lekki, Lagos
findings.summary: Mothercare, operated in Nigeria by SmartMark, has confirmed the opening of a new store at Purple Mall, Lekki on 29 August 2026, extending the brand's Lagos footprint. Purple Mall is the retail component of Purple Real Estate Plc's mixed-use Purple Lekki development on Freedom Way, approximately 20,000 sqm, reported at a development value of around ₦80bn, combining retail, office, short- and long-stay residential, gym, spa and leisure. The signing is evidence of continued anchor-brand fill-out at a scheme commissioned by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. Nigeria has produced few date-verified findings across the recent report series, so this item also confirms the asset is trading normally following its 2025 safety closure and subsequent regulatory clearance.

findings.title: Nigeria: Lagos Safety Commission closure list reported to include Lekki malls
findings.summary: Recorded for context only and clearly outside the 90-day window. In early May 2026 the Lagos State Safety Commission sealed 12 buildings across the state, a list reported to include malls in Lekki and hotels in Ikeja. The item is retained because it is a recurring regulatory risk factor for Lagos retail assets and relevant background to the Purple Mall finding above, but the specific properties affected were not independently confirmed to Category A/B standard. No directory change is recommended on this item.
